# Requirements Document ## Introduction The `blog-enhanced` spec layers discovery, engagement, and reading-UX polish on top of the static blog shipped by `blog-core` (spec 3). Concretely it adds: 1. **Pagefind site search** — a build-time crawl of the already-deployed-to-`next start` site that produces a compressed WASM index, plus a client-side search component, plus the CI pipeline changes required to crawl after build. 2. **Series UI** — index-page series badges and a per-post series navigator that surface the `series` / `seriesOrder` frontmatter fields that `blog-core` already emits but does not display. 3. **Related posts** — a small "Related" rail at the bottom of a post computed at build time from tag/category overlap. 4. **Social share affordances** — bot-friendly share links (mailto + Twitter/X + LinkedIn + URL-copy) below each post. 5. **Reading progress bar** — a thin top-of-viewport bar that tracks the reader's scroll position through the post body. 6. **Auto-generated table of contents** — a per-post TOC built from the post's headings, sourced from the existing `rehype-slug` output without re-parsing MDX at runtime. 7. **Footnote / sidenote rendering** — the visible UI for footnotes that `remark-gfm` (already in `velite.config.ts`) parses but renders unstyled today, plus optional desktop-margin sidenote presentation. 8. **Copy-to-clipboard buttons on code blocks** — a button injected into each fenced code block's `
` wrapper that copies the source.

All eight features are deliverable on top of `blog-core`'s existing Velite collection, MDX pipeline, page routes, and CI dual-build topology. No schema fields are added (`series` / `seriesOrder` already exist per `velite.config.ts:84-85`). No new content types are introduced. The CI pipeline is *extended* (a third build step), not restructured.

**Explicit non-goals** (documented to scope the spec tightly):

- **Comments / Giscus** — listed as future vision in `product.md:104`; not in this spec.
- **Newsletter / email subscription** — also future vision in `product.md:103`; not in this spec.
- **Analytics** — `product.md:105` future vision; this spec is read-only static, no analytics.
- **Search across non-blog routes at launch** — Pagefind's crawl will physically index `/profile`, `/contact`, and any other server-rendered routes that exist at crawl time, but the launch search UI scopes results to blog posts only (Req 1.13). Site-wide search is a future toggle.
- **Atom or JSON Feed** — blog-core's RSS-only decision (Req 11.14 in blog-core requirements.md) stands.
- **Adding `series` / `seriesOrder` schema fields** — they already exist. This spec only consumes them.
- **A `related: [slug, slug]` frontmatter manual-override field** — out of scope per Req 4.1's deliberate "algorithmic only at launch" decision.

## Alignment with Product Vision

- **Markdown-first content (product principle #2)**: No new frontmatter fields. Series grouping, related posts, TOC, footnotes, and copy-to-clipboard all work from the existing post body and frontmatter without authoring overhead.
- **Simple to maintain (product principle #3)**: Pagefind indexes at build time from the already-rendered HTML — no separate index file to maintain, no per-post indexing flag.
- **Wide and spacious (product principle #1)**: The TOC and sidenotes use generous whitespace via Tailwind utilities; the search UI is presented in a modal/dialog so it doesn't compete with prose width.
- **Accessible (product principle #7)**: Search UI is a Radix UI `Dialog` (keyboard-navigable focus trap), the TOC uses semantic `
` with `aria-label`, footnotes preserve `remark-gfm`'s anchor + back-reference structure for screen readers, copy-to-clipboard buttons announce status via `aria-live`, and the reading progress bar is decorative with `role="presentation"` (Req 5.7) so it is not announced as a control.
- **Performance (product success metric #4)**: Pagefind ships ~50KB of JS + lazy-loaded WASM (per Pagefind docs). The reading progress bar, TOC scroll-spy, and copy-to-clipboard buttons are the only blog-side client JavaScript introduced by this spec; combined budget bounded by Req 9.3. The Next.js baseline JS (~60-85KB per tech.md) remains the dominant client cost.
- **Independence from platforms (business objective)**: Search runs client-side from a self-hosted index. No Algolia, no Google Site Search, no external search dependency.
- **Theme parity (cross-spec convention)**: Every new UI surface (search dialog, search results, TOC, copy buttons, share buttons, sidenotes, progress bar) renders correctly in both light and dark themes — verified by Req 8.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: Pagefind site search (build-time index + client UI)

**User Story:** As a visitor who half-remembers a post about a topic, I want a search box that finds it without me browsing tag pages, so that I can read the post immediately.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The `pagefind` npm package SHALL be added to `devDependencies` in `package.json`. Pagefind is used in two distinct roles in this spec: (a) the CLI `pagefind` binary that crawls a running site and emits the `pagefind/` static asset directory, and (b) the `@pagefind/default-ui` (or equivalent) WASM + JS module loaded at search-dialog-open time by the client-side search component. Both roles are satisfied by the single `pagefind` package per its current packaging; Design SHALL pin the exact package(s) imported.
2. The Pagefind index SHALL be generated by a CI/local-build pipeline of the form: `next build → next start → wait-for-readiness → pagefind --site .next/standalone/... (or appropriate output directory) → terminate next start`. Design SHALL pin (a) the exact directory Pagefind crawls, (b) the wait-for-readiness mechanism (e.g. an `http-get`-style check on `http://localhost:3013/` returning HTTP 200), and (c) the teardown sequence that ensures `next start` is killed even if Pagefind fails. The crawl SHALL target `http://localhost:3013` (matching the existing `next start` port from `package.json`'s `start` script). The index output directory SHALL be `public/pagefind/` so Next.js serves the index as static assets from the deployed site.
3. The Pagefind index SHALL be regenerated on every CI run that produces a production-mode build (currently CI Build 2 per `blog-core` Req 7.14). The index is NOT generated on Build 1 (preview-mode with `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1`) — draft posts SHALL NOT be searchable. Locally, a `pnpm build:search` script SHALL exist that runs the same `build → start → crawl → stop` sequence so authors can verify search results before pushing.
4. **CI integration is non-blocking at launch** (per decomposition design consideration on `blog-enhanced`): the Pagefind crawl step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` SHALL be added to the Build 2 step group with `continue-on-error: true`. A failed crawl SHALL NOT fail the CI run. The step name SHALL be the literal `"Pagefind crawl (Build 2)"` so the existing `scripts/verify-ci-topology.mjs` pattern (matches step names by literal string per the comment in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:14-15`) can be extended to assert the step exists in the expected position.
5. **Promotion to blocking** is OUT of scope for this spec and SHALL be a one-line follow-up (`continue-on-error: true` → `continue-on-error: false`, or removal of the key) once the step has run successfully on 3+ consecutive `main` branch deploys. The spec deliverable is the non-blocking integration plus a documented promotion procedure in `design.md` — NOT the promoted state itself. This avoids cascading deployment-failure risk during the bring-up window.
6. **Indexing scope — explicit `data-pagefind-body` and `data-pagefind-ignore` boundaries**:
    - The `
` element on `/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` (currently at `src/app/(site)/blog/[slug]/page.tsx:73`) SHALL carry `data-pagefind-body` so Pagefind indexes the post body, title, headings, and tags as a single searchable record.
    - The site header (`src/components/layout/site-header.tsx` or equivalent), the site footer, the `` `
    ` element on the post page (`src/app/(site)/blog/[slug]/page.tsx:91-99`), the `` footer, the ``, and the to-be-added Related Posts rail (Req 4) and Share Bar (Req 6) and TOC (Req 7) SHALL all carry `data-pagefind-ignore="all"`. This ensures search results contain prose content only — no menu items, no related-post titles appearing as if they were part of the source post.
    - **No `data-pagefind-body` on index, taxonomy, or non-blog routes**: `/blog`, `/blog/tags/[tag]`, `/blog/categories/[category]`, `/profile`, `/contact`, slash pages, and the landing page SHALL NOT carry `data-pagefind-body`. These pages render lists of content, not the content itself; indexing them would surface listing-page hits that duplicate the underlying post hits. Pages without `data-pagefind-body` are still crawled by Pagefind for link-following but produce no search records (per Pagefind docs).
    - **Draft posts**: the post page already renders only when `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` is set at build time (per blog-core Req 7). Because Pagefind crawls the production Build 2 (Req 1.3) which has `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS` unset, draft posts are physically absent from the crawled output and therefore absent from the index. **The `data-pagefind-body` attribute SHALL still be present on draft post bodies in case a future operator misconfigures the crawler to point at Build 1** — and a CI smoke check (Req 1.12) SHALL fail the build if the production index contains any post whose slug matches an existing draft.
7. **Tag and category preservation in the index**: each post record SHALL include the post's tags and categories as Pagefind metadata via `data-pagefind-meta="tags:"` and `data-pagefind-meta="categories:"` attributes on the `
    ` element (or via Pagefind's `data-pagefind-meta` attribute on the existing tag/category `
      ` elements scoped INSIDE the indexed body region — Design SHALL pin the exact attribute placement). This enables the search UI to display the matched post's tags alongside the result snippet without a separate frontmatter lookup.
8. **Frontmatter `description` preservation**: each post record SHALL include the post's `description` frontmatter field as Pagefind metadata via `data-pagefind-meta="description"` on a server-rendered hidden element inside the indexed body region (an HTML pattern Pagefind documents for surfacing frontmatter to results). The search UI displays this description as the result excerpt when the matched fragment is the post title (which has no surrounding context to excerpt naturally). Design SHALL pin the element shape (e.g. a `{post.description}` rendered inside the `
      ` before ``).
9. **Search UI component — client component with lazy WASM load**:
    - A `` client component SHALL be exported from `src/components/blog/site-search.tsx`. It SHALL render a search trigger button in the site header (placement: rightmost in the header nav row, before the existing theme toggle so it does not displace the toggle's known position) AND a Radix UI `Dialog` that opens on trigger click, `Cmd/Ctrl+K` keyboard shortcut, AND `/` keyboard shortcut (the latter scoped — see Req 1.10).
    - The dialog SHALL contain (a) a text input auto-focused on open, (b) a results list that updates as the user types, (c) keyboard navigation through results (Up/Down arrow, Enter to navigate, Escape to close), (d) a "no results" empty state when the query matches no records, (e) an "Initial" state shown before the user has typed anything (suggested copy: "Type to search posts" — exact copy pinned in Design), and (f) a tag/category facet display per result.
    - The Pagefind WASM module SHALL be dynamically imported (`await import('/pagefind/pagefind.js')` or the equivalent the package documents) **only on first dialog open** — not at page load, not at component mount. This keeps the dialog's open-on-first-keystroke latency acceptable on first use while ensuring zero search cost on page load.
    - The dialog SHALL be a portal rendered into `` (Radix Dialog default), with the existing site CSP (`next.config.ts:38-49`) accommodating the inline styles Radix uses (already permitted by `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`).
10. **`/` keyboard shortcut scoping**: the `/` shortcut SHALL be ignored when (a) the active element is an ``, `
